Published online:

Geographic focus:
    India, Russia (New Delhi; broader geopolitical scope: Ukraine, China, Iran, Middle East)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — references 2022 Ukraine invasion, Dec 2025 Putin visit, Aug 2026 SCO summit
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — imminent BRICS summit, near-term trade/energy/defence discussions
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — expanding India-Russia trade, defence, nuclear, and energy ties; Russia's growing share of Indian crude imports

Synopsis:
    Modi and Putin met in New Delhi ahead of the BRICS summit to deepen bilateral cooperation across energy, defence, critical minerals, and civil nuclear sectors. India continues to resist Western pressure to cut Russian energy imports, with Russian crude reaching a record 51% of Indian imports in July 2026. The article underscores India's strategic balancing act: maintaining affordable energy access while diplomatically nudging for Ukraine peace resolution.

Relevance: NO — focus is on India-Russia bilateral relations, energy trade, and geopolitics

Q02. Is the content confirming already known information or reporting very new/uncertain risks?
Risk score: 20 — India-Russia energy and defence ties deepening is a well-established, ongoing trend; no major surprises. The record 51% Russian crude share adds a notable data point but fits within the expected trajectory.
